title: Code Quality & Clean Architecture
summary: Essential principles for maintainable, readable, and refactor-safe codebases in modern software engineering.
keyPrinciples: Clarity over cleverness: write code for the developer who has to debug it at 3 AM.
Single Responsibility: every module, class, or function should have exactly one reason to change.
Pure functions and immutability: minimize side effects to make behavior deterministic and testable.

rules.title: Avoid Boolean Flag Arguments in Functions
rules.description: Passing boolean flags (e.g. `getUser(id, true)`) obscures intent and forces a single function to do two distinct things. Split into two dedicated functions instead.

badExample.explanation: At the call site, the boolean literal provides zero readability without inspecting the function signature.

goodExample.explanation: Each function has a clear, self-documenting contract and no internal branching on boolean flags.

rules.title: Return Early (Guard Clauses) Over Deeply Nested Conditionals
rules.description: Deep nesting creates cognitive overload. Use early guard returns to handle invalid inputs or edge cases upfront.

badExample.explanation: Mental overhead compounds with every indentation layer.

goodExample.explanation: Preconditions are validated at the top; happy path runs flat and unobstructed.

productionChecklist: Strict linting and formatting configured in pre-commit hooks (Biome or ESLint + Prettier).
Functions are generally kept under 30 lines and do exactly one conceptual thing.
Dead code, commented-out blocks, and unused variables are pruned before merging.
Error cases return typed error objects or throw descriptive custom error classes.
